title: Predictive fleet slope allocator and quiet-window metering
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: We continue to see oscillatory behavior when fleets respond to multi-tenant bursts: rapid scale-ups followed by aggressive scale-downs create thrashing and missed short-lived capacity needs. This PR introduces a predictive slope allocator that smooths admission of new reservation capacity based on short-term utilization trends and a 'quiet-window' metering mechanism to suppress noisy utilization spikes from triggering immediate aggressive actions.

Goals: 1) Reduce autoscaler oscillation and unnecessary provisioning churn, 2) Preserve headroom for short-lived bursts by avoiding premature scale-downs, 3) Improve utilization signal fidelity by tagging and smoothing noisy tenants.

What this PR does (high level): Adds a new controller (pkg/autoscaler/slope_allocator.go) and a lightweight metering pipeline (pkg/telemetry/quiet_window_meter.go). The slope allocator computes a predictive slope over multiple percentiles (p50/p90/p99) of recent utilization windows and converts that slope to a softened reservation admission curve. The quiet-window meter applies tenant-level dampening: short spikes under configurable duration and amplitude thresholds are suppressed from contributing to global fleet signals.

Checklist: - [x] Implement core slope allocator and unit tests - [x] Integrate quiet-window metering into fleet-level aggregator - [x] Add e2e smoke integration in perf-canary harness - [x] Add dashboards and SLO alerts for new metrics - [x] Document configuration knobs and rollout plan - [x] Observability: histograms/gauges and debug traces included

Compatibility notes: Default behavior is opt-in by config flag (autoscaler.predictive_slope.enabled=false). When enabled, operators can tune smoothing coefficients, lookback duration, and spike suppression thresholds. There are no data migrations.

Performance/Cost: The added computation is O(N) per aggregation window where N is number of active tenants in a pool; we added local caching and work-slicing to keep single-controller CPU impact under 1 CPU for 10k tenants in our stress profile.

Rollout instructions: 1) Enable feature flag in a single non-critical fleet for one hour, 2) Observe metrics (slope_allocator.scale_rate, quiet_window.suppressed_spikes, autoscaler.thrashing_events), 3) Gradually enable on additional pools with conservative smoothing (alpha=0.15), 4) After 72h promote to default. See rollout_plan field for more detail.

Risks and mitigations: Over-smoothing could delay needed capacity during genuine ramp-ups. We mitigate by bounding softening factor and adding an emergency bypass path if p99 utilization exceeds emergency_threshold for two consecutive windows. The emergency path is tested in integration.

Related work: Builds on prior autoscaler PRs (ENG-31102 style warm-pool improvements) but focuses on signal quality and admission pacing rather than capacity sizing. Linked Linear items ENG-4271/ENG-4490 track follow-ups for multi-window aggregation and tenant fingerprinting.

release_notes: Adds a predictive slope allocator to smooth fleet reservation admissions and a quiet-window metering pipeline to reduce noisy spike influence on autoscaling decisions. Feature is disabled by default and gated by autoscaler.predictive_slope.enabled. See docs/ops/predictive-slope-allocator.md for tuning and rollout guidance.
risk_assessment: Medium: algorithmic changes affect admission pacing. Mitigations: opt-in default, emergency bypass path, conservative defaults, canary rollout and dashboards. Unit + integration tests added.
rollout_plan: 1) Enable in test cluster and run perf-canary smoke for 4h. 2) Enable on single non-critical fleet for 1h with alpha=0.10 and observe suppressed_spikes and thrashing_events. 3) If stable, incrementally enable additional pools over 72h. 4) Lower alpha slowly towards 0.25 only after verifying no increased latency or thrashing.
testing: Unit tests cover slope computation and admission mapping, component tests for quiet-window suppression, end-to-end perf-canary smoke shows reduced thrash in synthetic multi-tenant workload, manual verification of emergency bypass using stress tool. Logs and traces instrumented for debugging.
observability_changes: New metrics: slope_allocator.scale_rate (gauge), slope_allocator.admission_curve_factor (gauge), quiet_window.suppressed_spikes (counter), quiet_window.suppressed_by_tenant{tenant}. Added Grafana dashboard 'Autoscaler / Predictive Slope' and alerts for high thrashing_events and unexpected emergency_bypass_rate.
perf_impact_estimate: Controller CPU < 1 CPU at 10k tenants in our stress run; memory increase ~10MB for short-term sliding windows. Expected to reduce unnecessary fleet churn by ~12-18% in simulated multi-tenant burst tests.
